intended_object: The degree-0 Tate-cohomology deflation map Ĥ⁰(G/S, A^S) → Ĥ⁰(G/T, A^T) for nested normal subgroups S ≤ T with finite quotients, written on the cokernels of the norm maps: A^G / N_{G/S}(A^S) → A^G / N_{G/T}(A^T), induced by the identity of A^G. Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation ("finite-level deflation in Tate degrees −1 and 0 … gives maps between their kernels and cokernels") and the companion lemma `finiteZeroDeflationCokernel_π`.
explanation:
The definition applies `cokernel.map` to a commutative square of norm maps. One side of the square is the coinvariant deflation `finiteNegativeDeflationCoinvariants`, which is H₀-deflation; on generators it is the residual T/S norm. The other side is the identification of the total invariants (A^S)^{G/S} ≅ A^G ≅ (A^T)^{G/T}. The lemma `finiteNegativeDeflationCoinvariants_norm` proves that the square commutes. This uses N_{G/S} = N_{G/T} ∘ N_{T/S}, which is also what makes N_{G/S}(A^S) ⊆ N_{G/T}(A^T).

So the induced map on cokernels is the natural map A^G/N_{G/S}A^S → A^G/N_{G/T}A^T, which is the standard degree-0 map between Tate groups in this direction. The lemma `finiteZeroDeflationCokernel_π` confirms that the map is the invariants identification followed by the cokernel projection.

The definition is an intermediate layer: it is the cokernel model of Ĥ⁰, which is later transported to the library's Tate cohomology groups. The map itself is still a genuine mathematical object.

The generality is right: any commutative ring R, any group G, and normal subgroups with finite quotients. The extra instance `Fintype (T.map (mk' S))` only supplies data, since that subgroup is a subgroup of the finite group G ⧸ S. Mathlib has no Tate cohomology or deflation maps in Tate degree 0, so there is no counterpart.
